problem: Map-based navigation agents pretrained in noiseless simulators degrade under visual corruptions and dynamics noise (odometry and actuation) in new environments. Existing adaptation needs ground-truth supervision, or a known noise model (domain randomization), or fixed round-trip trajectories (GMC).
motivation: Ground-truth labels are unavailable in the real world, and the noise model of each deployment cannot be known in advance. Maps have strong structural regularities (flat walls, rectangular obstacles) and are a domain-agnostic interface between perception and policy, so these regularities can serve as a self-supervision signal and only the perception modules need fine-tuning.
key_idea: Train unpaired CycleGAN style-transfer networks on ego and global occupancy maps to turn noisy maps into clean-style pseudo-labels, then use them as self-supervised losses to fine-tune the mapping and localization models in a visual-then-dynamics curriculum.
insight: Structural priors from clean simulator maps can supervise both mapping (via ego maps) and localization (via global maps), because pose errors show up as structural distortions in the global map. The ablation on speckle noise shows the losses act at different stages: flip consistency mainly helps PointNav (success 0.12 to 0.20), and L_tc gives a large jump (success 0.20 to 0.42, pose xy 0.16 to 0.04 m). Adding the global style loss gives the best result (success 0.56, SPL 0.47). Adaptation works without round-trip trajectories, unlike GMC.
method: Map-based agent (Active Neural SLAM): mapping model f_M predicts an egocentric map from RGB, localization model f_L predicts pose from odometry and consecutive ego maps, and the global map is accumulated. Only f_M and f_L are fine-tuned; the policy stays frozen.

Unpaired map-to-map translation: CycleGAN trained between clean maps D_gt from the simulator and noisy maps D_noisy collected by the deployed agent. S_ego is trained on explored-area maps and S_global on obstacle maps.
Ego style transfer loss: L2 between predicted ego map m_t and S_ego(m_t), which adapts the mapping model to visual corruptions.
Flip consistency loss: the feature extractor output on a horizontally flipped RGB observation should equal the flipped output on the original, which stabilizes visual adaptation.
Global style transfer loss: L2 between global map M_t and S_global(M_t), which back-propagates through the pose to fine-tune the localization model against dynamics noise.
Temporal consistency loss: L2 between M_t and M_{t-1}, since earlier global maps carry less accumulated pose error.
Curriculum: collect noisy maps up to T_c and learn the style networks, then adapt visually up to T_v, then adapt dynamics up to T_d, all online and self-supervised.

setting.backbone: Active Neural SLAM agent (CNN mapping and pose estimator, frozen policy), pretrained on Gibson and fine-tuned; CycleGAN for map style transfer
setting.training_data: Pretrained on the Gibson train split with GT supervision; adaptation is self-supervised on unlabeled online maps from unseen Gibson or Matterport3D scenes, with clean map set D_gt from the simulator
setting.action_space: discrete Forward / Turn Left / Turn Right, planned from the global map
setting.privileged: none at adaptation time (no GT poses or maps); the clean map set D_gt comes from the noiseless simulator

numbers_note: Custom adaptation benchmarks in Habitat, not standard PointNav leaderboards. Success and SPL are printed as fractions (0.56), so they are copied as printed; the instructions would scale them to 0-100 but they are kept as printed to match the tables. Specialization for low-lighting is omitted here (SR 0.54, SPL 0.47, pose 0.06 m / 3.24°).
results: MoDA improves localization, mapping, exploration and PointNav over no adaptation, domain randomization, PAD and GMC in all three environments. For example, with speckle noise on Gibson its PointNav success/SPL is 0.56/0.47 versus GMC's 0.36/0.29 and NA's 0.12/0.10. On Matterport3D success is 0.22 versus GMC's 0.10. PAD gets slightly lower pose error in some settings but worse mapping and PointNav.
limitations: Only the perception modules (mapping and localization) are adapted; the policy is frozen and assumed to be domain-agnostic.
Requires an initial data collection phase to train CycleGAN style networks before adaptation, and evaluation is only in simulation with synthetic noise (no real robot).
Structural map priors assume regular indoor layouts and a shared clean map distribution; absolute Matterport3D PointNav success remains low (0.22).
